steps.content: After what happened at the hospital, you keep close tabs on Murphy. You learn that the old lady, whose bad luck turned out to be a blessing, later sent Murphy a commendation banner. With such recognition from a citizen, Murphy begins progressing steadily at her job.
One evening, you receive a photo from Murphy. It shows two tickets to an amusement park.

Chief! My boss gave me these two amusement park tickets! Hehe, I only got praised thanks to your help, so please, let me thank you properly! Are you free tomorrow? Let's go have a fun day out together!
You see no reason to say no. You wrap up your remaining work and clear your schedule for tomorrow.
[Scene Change]

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Good morning, Chief!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Good morning. You look energetic. I take it the trip here went smoothly?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Pretty good! The taxi driver only got lost for like fifteen minutes, the subway was delayed for another fifteen, and I only sprained my ankle a little on the walk here. Nothing major!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I promised you that you'd see a brand new Murphy, didn't I? Look, I wrote down everything we're going to do. Whatever happens today, I'm going to check all the items on my list with a smile!
Murphy waves the notebook in her hand. The page she has open reads: Itinerary - Amusement Park Day with Chief.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You even made an itinerary? Let me see...
#1: Try the park's famous strawberry sundae with Chief...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: You forgot to turn on the freezer last night and all the ice cream melted? No worries! Do you guys have bowls and straws? I'll just buy one and drink it like a milkshake.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Isn't the texture too thick? Maybe dilute it with some water.
#2: Get a unique balloon from the balloon vendor...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Chief, look! The balloon ribbon got completely tangled in my hair! That makes a pretty cool hairstyle, huh?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Let me untangle it for you.
#3: How can an amusement park trip be complete without some great pictures? We must take some pics with the mascots...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Sure, the dozen pictures we took all came out blurry... but at least this one of me falling on the ground is clear! I'm putting it on my desk!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Send me those image files. I can perhaps salvage a few of the blurry ones...
#4: Go to the water park and try the water seesaw.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Isn't that for kids? Are you sure two adults can even fit on it?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Come to think of it, why is the roller coaster the only thing not on this list? Most people come to the park for these thrill rides.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Th-thrill rides, huh...
Murphy turns her head away sheepishly.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: You know how I am. If I got on a roller coaster, I'd probably end up getting everyone else hurt...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I mean... I do really want to try them, but let's just stick to the other stuff for now.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Okay.
After that, you visit some other attractions, checking off items from Murphy's list one by one. By evening, as you head back toward the exit, you come across a little girl crouched by the side.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Hey there, what are you doing here?

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: I... don't know where Mommy and Daddy went. Do you know where the guest services desk is? Mommy and Daddy told me to go there if I got lost, but I can't find it anywhere.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Guest services... Um, I'm not great with directions, but it shouldn't be too hard to find. Let's look for it together, alright?

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: Okay!
Reassured, the girl joins you. The three of you begin following the signs toward the guest services desk.

But somehow, no matter how carefully you follow the directions, you can't find any trace of your destination. You only encounter more signs pointing in the opposite direction. Walking in an endless loop, you seem to keep barely missing the guest services desk.

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: Mommy and Daddy must not want me anymore... That's why I can't find it... Boohoo...
As she speaks, the little girl crouches down on the ground again, covering her eyes as she sobs.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Hey now, don't cry! We're just a little unlucky, that's all. Trust me when I say I know all about it!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Oh, I know! Let me tell you about all the unlucky things that've happened to me! Lots of people find these stories comforting!
Drawn in by Murphy's promise, the girl obediently lowers her hands and sniffles.
[Insert flashback, monologue, young Murphy's portrait]

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Ever since I was little, I've been super unlucky. There were a lot of kids in my family, and I was just the most ordinary one. I didn't get much attention.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Well, what could I do? I wasn't the cutest, and I wasn't the most likable either. Whenever they talked about me, they'd say I was the most sensible and easygoing child. I figured... that was at least a compliment, right? So I kept it up!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: But later on... things got worse. My exam scores were always one point short of the university cutoffs. I was the only one in my entire dorm with a different major. And when I took the civil service exam, I got assigned the job with the most unattractive package.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Everyone around me treated me like a walking disaster. They all kept their distance, terrified my bad luck would rub off on them. And then things got even worse... I contracted a <color=#dg1f1f>very strange illness</color>! I finally made a friend at work, but because of me, something terrible happened to her...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: So after that, I didn't even have anyone to talk to anymore. I had to constantly worry about causing problems for everyone around me. And even now, I don't have a single friend!
[End of flashback monologue]

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...So? See, I'm way unluckier than you, right? Now that you've heard all that, do you feel a little better?

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: Um...

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: All these bad things must make you feel really sad. So why aren't you crying?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Cry?

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: If I were you, I would've cried my eyes out.

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: But you're not crying, and you're telling me all this to make me feel better... Are you holding back your tears? That must be really hard...
The girl's small hand reaches up to touch Murphy's eyes. Suddenly, her vision blurs. The smile on her face finally crumbles, twisting into something even more pained than a crying face.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Wow... Do kids these days all sound like they're grown-ups?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Murphy, your bad luck might have accidentally comforted people in your work at the Public Security Bureau, but when you bare your wounds to others like that... it hurts you too, doesn't it?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The bad luck you had as a child, and the Mania you contracted as an adult... none of it was your fault. These are real scars you carry, not hardships that should be brushed aside, and they don't need to become entertainment for others. If those things still sting, then let it all out.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Curse them as harshly as you want. This isn't the office. You don't have to worry about who's listening. Just let it all out.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Cough...
Murphy fumbles for words, her voice trembling. She glances at you, then at the girl, before finally tilting her head back to stare up at the sky.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...I want to ride the roller coaster.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Now? Where's this coming from?
Murphy looks like she's about to burst into tears. Her M-value isn't particularly high right now though, so riding the roller coaster shouldn't be dangerous.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright then. My job today is to make sure you have a good time, after all.
The little girl beside you tugs at your sleeve, asking cautiously.

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: I want to ride the roller coaster too, but Mommy thinks it's too dangerous and won't let me. Can I come with you?

You glance at the roller coaster in the distance. It's not particularly tall, so it shouldn't be too dangerous. You steal a quick look at the figure behind you. Even if something does go wrong... you should be able to handle it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright then. I'll accompany you two brave ladies on this roller coaster ride.
You head back to the thrill ride area. Fortunately, the girl's height clears the 1.2-meter mark. She's tall enough to ride.

After the staff completes their checks, the roller coaster slowly begins its ascent into the sky. Eastside's night view unfolds before you. The car pauses briefly at the peak, then plunges into its thrilling descent.
As the wind roars past your ears during the dive, you hear the girl beside you let out a raw, cathartic scream.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Screw you, bad luck! Screw you, Mania! And screw my boss for dumping all the annoying tasks on me! You can all go to hell!!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I want friends too! I want people to care about me too! I want to be happy every single day too!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So that's why you suddenly wanted to ride the roller coaster. You're really letting it all out.

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: My stupid parents don't even care about me! They just want to be all lovey-dovey... Screw... Mmph!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Uh-uh, you shouldn't say that.
Amid the roaring wind and the screams of the other riders, you clamp your hand over the child's mouth to cut her off. Having finished their own venting, the two turn simultaneously to look at you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sigh... Alright, my turn.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Screw you, Black Ring! Screw you, the Underground! I'll eliminate all of you!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: That's the spirit! Woohoo, screaming at the sky from way up here feels incredible!
As if "something" has been eavesdropping on your conversation, the roller coaster grinds to a halt with a loud creak before Murphy can even finish her sentence, leaving you suspended in midair.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Oh no, we're... screwed. I knew it. I never should've gotten on this thing.
Fortunately, you've stopped at a relatively low point on the track and are right-side up, so you can all still breathe alright.
More and more visitors notice something's wrong with the roller coaster and gather below to watch. Among the onlookers, the child spots two familiar faces. She tugs on Murphy's arm.

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: That's... Mommy and Daddy! I found them!

steps.speaker: Lost Child's Mother
steps.content: Oh my goodness, how did you get up there?! Somebody, please help get my child down right now!!

steps.speaker: Roller Coaster Operator
steps.content: We're very sorry! Everyone, please remain calm and stay still! There's been a minor system error. I'll reset it right away... Just a moment!
A few minutes later, with a hum in the tracks, the roller coaster starts moving again. You make it back to the starting point unharmed, your aerial adventure finally over.
Back on solid ground, the lost child rushes into her anxious parents' arms. She pounds her little fists against them a few times before bursting into tears.

steps.speaker: Lost Child's Mother
steps.content: I'm so sorry for all the trouble. Thank you both for looking after her. Sweetie, say thank you.

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: Thank you for taking care of me. Sorry for the trouble.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Not at all! She's such a sweet, empathetic kid. If anything, I should be thanking her.
Murphy waves her hand bashfully, then crouches down and whispers something into the girl's ear.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Those things I told you about are all in the past. But now? I've met this gentleman here, and so many other people just like me. These days have been the luckiest time of my entire life!
steps.female_content: Those things I told you about are all in the past. But now? I've met this lady here, and so many other people just like me. These days have been the luckiest time of my entire life!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: So, keep being the awesome girl you are, okay? Your bad luck won't last forever. Our lucky days are still waiting for us down the road, right?

steps.speaker: Lost Child
steps.content: Mmm!
Murphy watches the family walk away, her gaze following them into the distance. Perhaps reminded of her own past, she seems quietly moved.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Feel better after screaming it all out? If that's not enough, you can cry like she did, you know.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Chief, what are you talking about? I didn't even dare to cry like that when I was little. Now that I'm all grown up... isn't it a bit too late for that?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Well, growing up didn't make your bad luck go away or solve your problem, did it? Both the unlucky little girl and the unlucky big girl have the right to cry about it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Since you can't change it, you might as well face it with a smile. But complaining works too. So does crying. Who says adults aren't allowed to cry?
You say and open your arms, offering her an embrace.
She throws herself into your arms and finally bursts into tears.
Murphy cries in your arms for a long time. When she finally stops, the sky is already dark.
You head toward the park's exit, retracing the path you took on the way in. Behind you, fireworks bloom across the sky. You both stop to watch as brilliant colors shine upon your faces and eyes.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: How beautiful... I knew today would be my lucky day. I'm so happy I got to come here with you, ${PlayerName}.
She takes out her notebook and begins jotting down something carefully.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Recording your good luck and bad luck again?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Well... yes and no! This time I'm not going to write down everything, and I'm not going to categorize them as good or bad either! I just want to note down the happy moments I had today.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Maybe from now on, I'll keep doing it this way... Let the insignificant details fade away, and only record the things that make me happy! That way when I look back, I can feel more at ease.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Good idea. And if someday you feel like letting it all out again, you're always welcome to come find me at the Bureau. Just remember to give me a heads-up. We've already gone over our repair budget.
Murphy puffs out her cheeks and shoots you a look.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Chief, remember that piggy bank metaphor you mentioned before? You said good luck and bad luck are both just little coins dropped inside.
As she speaks, she traces the shape of a piggy bank in the air with her hands.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I'm ready! From now on, I'm only going to save the good luck! As for everything else... who cares if they're good or bad? A thing is good if I decide it is!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Since my bad luck is everywhere anyway, I might as well just pretend it's nowhere at all... right?
She says and sticks her tongue out at you playfully.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Everything went according to my itinerary today! We checked off everything on the list! I'm really, really happy. Thank you, Chief!
After bidding you farewell, Murphy leaves clutching her notebook, waving at you enthusiastically the whole way.
Once the red-haired girl's figure finally vanishes from sight, two figures emerge from the shadows.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Looks like we won't need to execute Plan B after all.
[Insert Flashback]

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You mean I should take Murphy back to the Bureau for supervision if she fails to meet the standard?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Yes. Her ability is quite unique. If her mental state can't be stabilized, the resulting bad luck will pose a serious threat to civilians around her.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: You can meet with Murphy today as planned. I'll secretly observe her mental state and behavior. I'll bring sufficient backup to subdue her, should it come to that. If she fails to meet the standard by the end of the day, we'll have no choice but to bring her back to the Bureau.
[End of Flashback]

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: When it comes to guiding Sinners and placing your full trust in them, no one can beat you, Chief. I admit I was wrong to doubt you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: To be honest, I'm surprised at how far she's come in such a short time too.
Perhaps, in some mysterious way, "fate" finally smiled upon her and lent a hand.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Hey, hey, hey, what about me? So I came all the way here for nothing? I spent the whole day watching you two eat delicious snacks and go on rides, while I was stuck on standby munching stale bread. Is that even fair?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Not having to fight should be a good thing, no? Don't tell me you were actually hoping for some action?

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: I don't care! I came all the way to the park, so either let me throw some punches, or come with me again tomorrow to play. I deserve some kind of reward!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll pass. The park just barely survived the Goddess of Bad Luck. Having the Archer Queen show up right after would be too much for them to handle. This isn't the Bureau, after all.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: ...Uh, worst joke I've ever heard!
At EMP's remark, all three of you burst into laughter.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright, alright. Since we're already here, let's stay for the fireworks at least. There are food stalls nearby too. My treat—eat as much as you want.
Despite everything, this could have turned out so much worse.
You hope Murphy's Mania can treat her with more kindness from now on.
And perhaps more mercy from "fate"—which has been so exceptionally hard on her—too.
